title: Boeuf Bourguignon
subtitle: Burgundy-braised beef with bacon, mushrooms, and pearl onions
excerpt: The great Burgundy stew: beef braised in a full bottle of red wine with bacon lardons, chestnut mushrooms, and pearl onions until the meat is tender enough to cut with a spoon and the sauce is dark, glossy, and rich.

recipe.sourceNotes: Boeuf bourguignon is one of the most celebrated dishes of French cuisine, originating in Burgundy where both the wine and the cattle are exceptional. It was popularised in Britain and the United States largely through the work of Julia Child, whose recipe in Mastering the Art of French Cooking (1961) became the definitive version for generations of home cooks. The dish is a classic braise: tough cuts of beef braised slowly in wine until the collagen in the meat converts to gelatin and the sauce thickens.

recipeTools.notes: Enamelled cast iron works best for this braise.

content.text: Brown the beef in batches and do not skimp on this step. The colour you build at the browning stage goes directly into the final flavour of the sauce. The wine does the rest, but only if the meat is well browned first. The dish improves overnight: make it the day before and reheat gently, which deepens the sauce and makes it easier to skim the fat.

items.preparation: a full bottle of Burgundy or robust red

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Pat the beef dry and season well. Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the beef in 3 batches for 3 to 4 minutes per batch, without moving. Remove each batch and set aside.

Add the lardons to the casserole and cook for 4 minutes until lightly browned. Add the shallots and carrots and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato puree, and flour and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and scrape up any browned bits. Add the stock, herbs, and browned beef. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook in the oven for 2 to 2.5 hours until the beef is very tender and the sauce has reduced and thickened.

Fry the mushrooms in the butter in a frying pan over high heat for 5 minutes until golden. Add to the stew for the last 30 minutes of cooking. Remove the herb stalks. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread.
